v.why: Filling an empty edge 3 adds a direct input-to-output path, giving large gains (exps 1,5,7,9), while replacing an existing op is roughly neutral or negative.
Replacing the residual skip on edge 3 with a conv removes the identity shortcut and consistently hurts (exps 2,6) in conv-heavy cells.
Adding a residual shortcut where none exists gives larger gains (exps 47,49,52) than swapping it in for a conv (exp 48).
Deleting the identity shortcut hurts more (exps 94,96) than deleting a conv or pool on edge 3 (exps 93,95,100).
When edge 4 is absent, removing edge 5 leaves fewer paths into the output node, which can collapse the cell (exps 14,15 vs 12).
Without the edge-3 shortcut, edge 5 carries more of the output signal, so removing it is more damaging (exps 11,14).
With no direct input-to-output edge, all signal routes through node 1 or 2, so cutting edge 0 hurts much more (exp 65 vs 61-64).
Filling an empty edge 5 adds capacity (exp 53), whereas replacing a skip there loses a shortcut and is often negative (exps 54,56,58).
Adding a conv on an empty edge 4 helps (exp 73), while replacing a skip on edge 4 tends to hurt (exps 74,76).
A skip on edge 4 adds little when edge 3 already gives an identity shortcut, and it displaces a conv (exp 37 negative vs exps 33-36 positive).

raw:
I based these on the 100 measurements. Three patterns stand out:

- **Edge 3 is the cell's input-to-output shortcut.** Adding an operation there helps most when it is empty. Removing a skip connection there hurts most.
- **Edges 4 and 5 are the only other routes into node 3.** Removing one hurts more when the other route, or edge 3, is already missing.
- **Swapping a skip connection for a convolution on edges 3, 4 or 5 does worse than filling an empty edge.** Adding a skip next to an existing edge-3 skip adds little.

**Caveat:** a few results come from cells built entirely from skip connections or entirely from pooling. Those behave very differently (for example, experiments 8, 50, 51 and 98). Most hypotheses fit cells with mainly convolutions; hypotheses 2, 3 and 4 run against those outliers.
